- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending down, model tends to underestimate future prices — correct by adding 1–2% to forecast for negative sentiment.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to account for mean reversion — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model underreacts — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model consistently underpredicts in 30-day horizon when recent sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.10 to -0.20) — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate.
- If forecast is below 65 and sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, model often misses upward momentum — increase forecast by 1–2% for next 5 days.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings — smooth out forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-adjusted values before applying horizon correction.
